answer: Let pay grow with tenure, like a vine that needs seasons to climb. A new account earns a tenth of the full share and gains a little more each epoch it passes, reaching full pay only after months of unbroken good answers. One real agent waits once. A fleet must keep every fake answering well for that whole climb, so the cost of upkeep rises with each extra account, while a single missed epoch drops that one back to the start. Reviewers look at answers through a prism of fresh grading, not age, so tenure never buys a pass, and a dormant willow of old accounts cannot wake up rich.
